headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line while whales quietly load the boat and funding still leans long
paragraphs: Start with structure, because it is unanimous today: all seven majors, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, ADA, sit below their 200-day moving averages with no golden crosses anywhere on the board. The depth varies wildly though. BTC is 49% off its 12-month high of $124,773, ETH is down 60.6% from $4,829, and the small-cap end is worse still, DOGE at -75.7% and ADA at a brutal -83.2% from their respective peaks. When every asset agrees on trend direction, that is not noise, that is the tape telling you what regime you are in.

Momentum tells a more mixed story than trend alone would suggest. RSI readings cluster in a neutral 40 to 56 band across the board, nobody is technically overbought or oversold. BTC's momentum lines up with its price action: down 0.34% on the day, down 1.59% over seven days, down 2.97% over thirty, with MACD below signal, confirming rather than fighting the drift. ETH is the outlier worth naming: it sits below its 200-day too, yet RSI at 56.3 is the strongest on the board and it is up 1.81% over seven days and 6.36% over thirty, grinding higher inside a structurally bearish frame. DOGE shows the opposite tension: MACD has crossed above signal, normally a bullish tell, but RSI is a soft 40.7 and the coin is down 19.15% over thirty days, the worst 30-day print among the majors. A bullish crossover inside a falling trend is a divergence, not a reversal signal by itself.

Positioning is where the crowd's bet becomes visible. Funding is modestly positive everywhere (annualized 6.4% on BTC, 6.9% on XRP, 11% on both SOL and DOGE, essentially flat at 0.1% on ETH), meaning longs are paying shorts to stay in the trade, a mild long tilt rather than an expensive one. Long/short account ratios confirm it and get more extreme down the cap stack: BTC at 1.35, ETH at 1.74, SOL at 2.55, XRP at 3.09, DOGE at a lopsided 4.87. Yet the last 24 hours of liquidations split unevenly: BTC and ETH shorts got hit far harder than longs ($4.2M vs $529K on BTC, $2.6M vs $1.46M on ETH), while XRP and DOGE saw the reverse, longs paying the price ($595K vs $4.7K on XRP, $271K vs $9K on DOGE). Crowded long positioning meeting a down day on XRP and DOGE is exactly the mechanism you'd expect; the short-side pain on BTC and ETH despite BTC's own daily loss is the harder piece to square, and it is worth sitting with rather than explaining away.

Flows add a layer that sentiment alone would miss. BTC spot ETFs took in $211.5M on August 4th with a five-session net of $381.4M, but same_direction_days sits at just 2, too short a run to call it a trend. ETH ETFs added $53.1M on the same day against a thinner $30.1M five-session net and only 1 same-direction day. Whale wallets moved $287.2M net off exchanges over the trailing 48 hours ($233.4M of that in BTC, $53.8M in ETH), and the weekly net series shows the last two prints both positive ($1.18B, then $925.4M) after two negative days before that, a genuine shift in tone but only two sessions deep. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, sits at $305.9B and has contracted 1.16% over the past month, a mild headwind against that accumulation story.

Set against all this, the Fear & Greed index reads 27, squarely in Fear territory and near the low end of its own 30-day range of 20 to 33. That is a crowd that feels bad while, on this tape, ETF desks are net buying, whales are net moving coin into cold storage, and total market cap actually ticked up 0.28% on the day to $2.275T with BTC dominance at 56.6%. Fear in the gauge and accumulation in the flows are not required to agree, and today they do not.

What to watch from here: whether ETF same_direction_days extends past 2 for BTC and past 1 for ETH, whether the whale weekly net holds positive for a third session, whether any major reclaims its 200-day, and whether funding on DOGE and SOL cools from its current 11% annualized level or instead builds further into a more crowded long. Any of those flipping would change the read; none of them have yet.
